title: HTGTS
scope: Architecture of the supplied Illumina HTGTS explanatory schematic: one end-processed, adapter-first DNA-library route from genomic material to purified sequencing-end-tagged DNA. All eight depicted transformations and bead attachment are retained; no alternative branch or sequencing run is drawn. Biological joining is upstream context. Hu et al. Figure 1a supports interpretation of this implementation, while Chiarle et al. support the bait–prey principle but report different experimental library routes. Explicit repertoire and linear-amplification variants are qualified in method_scopes without importing unshown operations into the graph. Publication metadata and catalogue timestamps are not used to establish invention or priority.

evidence.locator: [b00005], Introduction: determinants of translocation frequency
evidence.quote: The frequency of translocations between two sites in the genome is a function of the frequency at which DSB ends at the two sites are available to be translocated and the frequency at which they are physically juxtaposed (“synapsed”)2. The frequency at which DSBs are available is influenced both by their rate of generation and by how long they persist before being rejoined2.

method_scopes.rationale: All eight operations belong to the single end-processed, adapter-first HTGTS route actually drawn, consistent with Hu et al. Figure 1a. It is an explanatory architecture, not the exact 2011 Chiarle implementation: that paper describes restriction-fragmented adapter-PCR and circularization-PCR libraries sequenced by Roche-454. Those unshown restriction/blocking/circularization routes are not added as branches. The biological target is a pre-existing bait–prey DNA junction, carried as copied genomic sequence in the final library.

method_scopes.rationale: Only genomic-DNA sonication is directly mapped, supported by the catalogue. That text then describes linear amplification with a biotinylated J-associated primer, enrichment of labeled ssDNA, and bridge-adapter ligation after capture; it is not the figure’s adapter-first route. The supplied Lin abstract establishes IgH/IgL V(D)J exon, CDR3 and DJH repertoire measurement using J primers. That is the supported target, rather than equating repertoire sequencing with AID-dependent class switching. The exact variant chemistry, especially the catalogue’s six-nucleotide UMI designation, is not verified by the abstract-only primary evidence. Other complete diagram operations are not assigned solely because names overlap.

jcr:content/par/text_1/text, repertoire variant description
evidence.quote: In HTGTS-Rep-seq, genomic DNA from B-cell populations is sonicated and linearly amplified with a biotinylated primer that anneals downstream of a J segment. The biotin-labeled single-stranded DNA products are enriched with streptavidin beads, and the 3’ ends are ligated to a bridge adaptor containing a 6-nucleotide UMI.
evidence.rationale: Catalogue-level chemistry claim. The supplied Lin paper is abstract-only; detailed primer, adapter and UMI chemistry has not been independently verified.

evidence.locator: Abstract only: assay target and J-primer selection
evidence.quote: We now describe an unbiased, sensitive, and readily accessible assay, referred to as high-throughput genome-wide translocation sequencing-adapted repertoire sequencing (HTGTS-Rep-seq), to quantify antibody repertoires. HTGTS-Rep-seq quantitatively identifies the vast majority of IgH and IgL V(D)J exons, including their unique CDR3 sequences, from progenitor and mature mouse B lineage cells via the use of specific J primers.

evidence.locator: Abstract only: DJH and productive/nonproductive configurations
evidence.quote: HTGTS-Rep-seq also accurately quantifies DJH intermediates and V(D)J exons in either productive or nonproductive configurations.

method_scopes.rationale: Sonication is the directly shared transformation. The full-text protocol separately establishes: linear amplification across a known bait into prey using a 5′ biotinylated primer; capture of resulting ssDNA on streptavidin beads; bridge-adapter ligation after capture; then nested and sequencing-end PCR. The depicted end-repair/A-addition/adapter-before-capture route is not assigned to this variant. Capture and PCR names overlap, but their material substrates differ, so they are not treated as identical graph operations. The card’s HTGTS CRISPR/Cas9 label denotes an application; the engineered-nuclease paper specifically supports a linear-amplification-mediated implementation for Cas9 and TALEN work, not a universal alias for every HTGTS CRISPR experiment.

corrections.primary_statement: Hu et al. explicitly distinguish LAM-HTGTS: linear amplification produces biotinylated ssDNA, enrichment occurs next, and bridge-adapter ligation follows enrichment. Only sonication is mapped to the same graph operation. The LAM sequence is described in its scope rather than replacing the drawing or asserting that shared operation names imply equivalent substrates.

evidence.quote: LAM-HTGTS directly amplifies junctions from sheared genomic DNA using LAM-PCR followed by enrichment and bridge adapter ligation to allow for exponential amplification and Miseq labeling of enriched products.

evidence.locator: [b00012], LAM-HTGTS overview: amplification, capture and ligation
evidence.quote: LAM-PCR with a single 5’ biotinylated primer amplifies across the bait sequence into the unknown prey sequence (Fig. 1b). Junction-containing ssDNAs are enriched via binding to streptavidin-coated magnetic beads (Fig. 1b). After washing, bead-bound ssDNAs are unidirectionally ligated to a bridge adapter18.

corrections.diagram_observation: The figure is labeled HTGTS and Breakage in genome, with no J segment, V(D)J exon, CDR3 or UMI label. The catalogue associates HTGTS-Rep-seq with AID-dependent IgH class switching.
corrections.primary_statement: The supplied Lin abstract defines HTGTS-Rep-seq as antibody-repertoire measurement using J primers to recover IgH/IgL V(D)J exons and CDR3 sequences, including DJH intermediates and productive/nonproductive configurations. That primary-supported target is used for this named variant. The abstract does not verify the catalogue’s detailed adapter/UMI chemistry or assign the entire figure to this variant.

jcr:content/par/text_1/text, application sentence
evidence.quote: This approach is particularly suitable for studying for AID-dependent IgH class-switching (HTGTS-Rep-seq) and CRISPR/Cas9 genome modifications.

evidence.locator: Abstract only: assay target and J-primer selection
evidence.quote: We now describe an unbiased, sensitive, and readily accessible assay, referred to as high-throughput genome-wide translocation sequencing-adapted repertoire sequencing (HTGTS-Rep-seq), to quantify antibody repertoires. HTGTS-Rep-seq quantitatively identifies the vast majority of IgH and IgL V(D)J exons, including their unique CDR3 sequences, from progenitor and mature mouse B lineage cells via the use of specific J primers.

evidence.locator: Abstract only: DJH and productive/nonproductive configurations
evidence.quote: HTGTS-Rep-seq also accurately quantifies DJH intermediates and V(D)J exons in either productive or nonproductive configurations.

unknowns.question: Does the six-nucleotide segment called a UMI by the catalogue remain in sequenced HTGTS-Rep-seq molecules as a molecule identifier, and what is its exact adapter/ligation role? The supplied Lin abstract does not specify adapter chemistry. Resolution requires that paper’s full-text or supplementary oligonucleotide/library architecture showing the ligated and retained strands. No UMI is assigned to the Illumina diagram meanwhile.
